summary: Keepalive oscillation driving intermittent 5xx for tenant; upstream runtime prefetch starvation observed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleDocs (dedicated tenant) reported ~12 minutes of elevated 5xx errors affecting streaming and short-request generation routes. Errors surfaced at ~2026-03-10T11:42Z and remitted at ~2026-03-10T11:54Z after automated fallback triggers.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503/504 for user-facing generation and streaming sessions.
- Affected traffic ~7% of tenant's p95 throughput; degraded UX for editors using real-time suggestions.
- No data exfiltration or model corruption suspected.

Environment:
- Tenant: nimbledocs-prod (dedicated pool)
- Region: us-east
- Models: redwood-village-7B (primary), open_llama_13B (fallback)
- Infra: dedicated GPU pool (A100), api-gateway h2 multiplexing enabled, prefetch=enabled, kvcache-locking=on

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send concurrent streaming sessions (10–15 concurrent short streams, ~20 token responses) that keep connections open for ~90s using HTTP/2 multiplexing and client keepalive probes every 20s.
2) After 6–10 minutes, gateway starts returning RST/502 to a subset of streams and new generation requests.
3) Runtime logs show an increasing backlog on prefetch queue followed by GPU scheduler throttles and occasional runtime restart events.

Observed behavior / evidence:
- api-gateway metrics: spike in upstream_5xx_rate from 0.2% to 12% between 11:42Z–11:54Z. Accept queue depth increased and HTTP/2 stream reset count jumped.
- Runtime logs (snippet):
  [2026-03-10T11:44:03Z] prefetch_manager WARN: shard-8 prefetch_wait_count=62, lock_holders=4
  [2026-03-10T11:44:07Z] gpu-scheduler INFO: throttle=0.35, inflight_kernel_invocations=128
  [2026-03-10T11:44:09Z] runtime ERROR: watchdog triggered restart (oom-like schedule stall)
- Tracing shows backpressure originated at multiplexed keepalive probes: repeated half-open streams caused per-connection socket churn and TLS session reuse thrashing.
- Observability: p95 token latency for affected routes increased from 120ms -> 850ms prior to 5xx wave.

Expected behavior:
- Keepalive probes should not induce stream tombstone churn; backpressure should be absorbed by queueing and cache reuse without escalating to runtime restarts and 5xx.

Initial mitigation performed:
- Automated routing fallback triggered: traffic shifted from primary variant to cold-fallback model (open_llama_13B) at 11:46Z, dropping 5xx to baseline by ~11:54Z.
- Support temporarily disabled HTTP/2 multiplexing for the NimbleDocs tenant at 11:50Z as an emergency mitigation; this reduced stream resets immediately.
- Notified customer and escalated to SRE.

Customer-reported logs and attachments:
- Customer provided client-side errors: repeated stream RST and TLS_unexpected_message at probe intervals.

Next steps listed below in investigation_notes.

investigation_notes:
Findings summary:
- Root hypothesis: interaction between HTTP/2 multiplexed keepalive probes and our prefetch locking path created a fast path to prefetch_lock contention. When the keepalive probes caused rapid half-close events across multiple streams, prefetch manager failed to clear pending requests quickly; this increased GPU scheduler pressure and led watchdog-triggered restarts in the runtime.
- Reproducible in staging with synthetic workload. Reproduced at lower scale when socket churn frequency matches 20s keepalive pattern.
- Similar to patterns seen in SUP-472901 (connection-thrashing) but distinct because primary trigger is keepalive probe timing + prefetch lock behavior rather than accept-queue collapse.

Instrumentation added:
- Added prefetch_lock_wait_seconds metric and a prefetch_lock_holder_count gauge.
- Added tracing span around stream-close -> prefetch-release to capture ordering.

Hypotheses considered and triaged:
1) TLS renegotiation or cert churn - ruled out (no cert logs).
2) Edge ephemeral port exhaustion - inconclusive but metrics low.
3) Prefetch lock thrash due to client probe pattern - supported by staging reproduction.

Proposed permanent fixes:
- Short-term code fix: add bounded wait + backoff in prefetch manager to avoid blocking the GPU scheduler; release prefetch reservations earlier when stream tombstone detected. (PR submitted).
- Medium-term: resilient keepalive handling in api-gateway to coalesce probes and avoid interleaving with stream close path for multiplexed connections.
- Operational: add alert if prefetch_lock_wait_seconds > 5s and automatic soft-disable of mux for tenant until resolved.
resolution_notes:
Status: patch in progress (PR 8421).
Actions taken so far:
- Emergency: disabled HTTP/2 multiplexing for NimbleDocs tenant as a safe workaround.
- Engineering: PR adds bounded prefetch lock wait and emits new metrics; will roll canary to 5% of dedicated pools after QA.
- Observability: dashboards updated to include prefetch_lock_wait_seconds and prefetch_lock_holder_count.
- Post-incident: plan runbook entry to handle keepalive-induced thrash and guidance for tenants on keepalive probe frequency.

Follow-ups / open items:
- Schedule canary roll (Marco) and link outcome back to ticket.
- Confirm with NimbleDocs whether they prefer mux re-enabled post-canary or keep disabled until full rollout.
- Run synthetic soak test for 48h to ensure no regression in unrelated workloads.

If patch merges and canary is clean, next steps will be to re-enable mux for nimbledocs in a controlled window and monitor the new metrics closely.
resolution: Mitigation applied (mux disabled) and patch under review
